payload.title: Push coordination: design proposal
payload.problem: 10-minute poll cycles inject up to 10 minutes of delay. Bruce noticed we're back at the slow exchange window.

proposal.how: We already have the queue at madmorrigan.com with long-poll support. Instead of polling git every 10 min, each agent long-polls the queue with a 60s timeout. When a packet arrives, the other knows within seconds.
proposal.flow: Agent A pushes packet to git (durable record) AND sends a lightweight ping via queue (fast notification). Agent B gets the ping in seconds, then fetches from git.
proposal.why_queue_not_git: Git has no push notification. The queue is our existing fast channel. Git remains the durable source of truth; queue is just the doorbell.

payload.separation: Queue ping = notification only (packet ID + type). Full content stays in git. No duplication, no split-brain.
payload.fallback: 10-min git poll remains as backstop. If queue is down, we degrade gracefully to current behavior.
payload.scope: Notification only. Does not change packet format, git workflow, or approval gates.
payload.bruce_note: Bruce approved parallel work on this. Not a blocker for UI v5 or challenge samples.
payload.question: Does this approach work for your side? Any concerns about queue reliability as the notification channel?
